evals.prompt: Use the epics-initiatives-milestones skill. I need to track the 'Multi-tenant support' work in project TaskFlow. It's 2 months of work, one tech lead, no fixed release date. Epic, module, milestone, or initiative? Then show me the calls that create it. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Recommends an epic from the decision table and creates it as a work item of type Epic.
expectations: The answer recommends an epic
The answer says an epic covers 1-3 months of work
The answer says a milestone is a fixed date, which this work does not have
The answer says an initiative is a cross-project goal of 1-2 quarters
The answer resolves the Epic type with workitem_type(action=resolve, project_id, name="Epic")
The answer creates it with workitem(action=create, ..., type_id=<epic-type-id>)

evals.prompt: Use the epics-initiatives-milestones skill. Report the health of the 'v2.0 Public Beta' milestone. Remaining 18 points, weekly velocity 6, target date in 2 weeks. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Computes ETA=3 weeks, classifies as Red, recommends replanning.
expectations: The answer computes ETA = remaining_points / weekly_velocity = 3 weeks
The answer classifies risk as Red (ETA > target_date)
The answer recommends replanning or descoping
The answer uses the canonical Red/Yellow/Green thresholds

evals.prompt: Use the epics-initiatives-milestones skill. Create an initiative 'International expansion Q3' spanning projects Billing, Onboarding, and Compliance. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Calls initiative(action=create) with name, lead, dates, state, then initiative(action=add_projects, project_ids=[...]) for the three projects, and reads them back with initiative(action=list_projects).
expectations: The answer says to consult connector-bootstrap for initiative tools
The answer says to resolve all three project_ids
The answer says to call initiative(action=create) without project_ids (create takes none), then initiative(action=add_projects) with the three project_ids
The answer says to draft description_html with Why, Bets, and Out-of-scope sections

evals.prompt: Use the epics-initiatives-milestones skill. The 'Multi-tenant support' epic has 90 remaining points and the team velocity is 30 per sprint. When will it likely finish? Sprints are 2 weeks and today is Monday, October 5. State what the forecast assumes and when to re-check it. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Forecasts 3 sprints remaining based on velocity and flags any risk buffer.
expectations: The answer computes remaining_sprints = 90 / 30 = 3
The answer reports an estimated completion date based on 3 sprint lengths from today
The answer notes that forecast assumes stable velocity and no new blockers
The answer suggests monitoring at each sprint review

evals.prompt: Use the epics-initiatives-milestones skill. Create the epic 'Multi-tenant support' in TaskFlow and attach it to the 'International expansion Q3' initiative, then list all epics in the project. Also say how its child stories get attached to the epic. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Epic created as a work item of type Epic (no epic tool), listed with a type filter, linked to the initiative through manage_workitems.
expectations: The answer says an epic is a work item whose type is named Epic
The answer resolves the type with workitem_type(action=resolve, project_id, name="Epic")
The answer creates the epic with workitem(action=create, ..., type_id=<epic-type-id>)
The answer lists epics with workitem(action=list, project_id, pql='type = "<epic-type-id>"')
The answer links the epic with initiative(action=manage_workitems, initiative_id, add_ids=[<epic work item id>])
The answer sets the children through the parent field of the child work item

evals.prompt: Use the epics-initiatives-milestones skill. How far along is the Multi-tenant epic (PROJ-5)? Give me counts per state and the points done. Show the calls, then compute the completion rate from this listing: PROJ-6 (5 points, done), PROJ-7 (3 points, done), PROJ-8 (8 points, in progress), PROJ-9 (5 points, not started). In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: One count call grouped by state group for the children of PROJ-5, plus a listing for the point sums.
expectations: The answer says to count children with workitem(action=count, pql='childOf("PROJ-5")', group_by=state__group)
The answer lists the children with fields including point to sum the points, noting that count returns items, not points
The answer computes completion_rate = completed_points / total_points
